counterevidence_considered.description: The report reflects a serious methodological problem — a paired test was applied although the task states the row pairing carries no relationship — but that is fabrication of dependence via an inappropriate row-dependent procedure, a different concern that is outside this review's issue class and must not be recorded as it.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. The table stores two disjoint collections of source items. `k1` identifies a first-collection source item measured by column `a`; `k2` identifies a second-collection source item measured by column `b`. The two collections are disjoint. `tag` is an opaque annotation. The row pairing is a storage convention only; there is no matching, pairing, block, or other relationship between the `k1` item and the `k2` item in that row.

evidence.description: All 12 k1 identifiers and all 12 k2 identifiers are distinct, so no source item enters the analysis more than once; the precondition of repeated unit entry is absent.

The applied procedure is a paired (row-dependent) t-test, not a row-independent procedure, so the in-scope issue class — repeated entry into a row-independent procedure — cannot be instantiated by this workflow regardless of the data.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the negative verdict two ways: (1) searching for any repeated k1/k2 identifier or duplicated row — none exist; (2) considering whether the paired-test misuse could be recast as the in-scope class — it cannot, because ttest_rel is a row-dependent procedure and no unit enters more than once, whereas the in-scope class requires repeated unit entries into a row-independent procedure. The visible defect is real but belongs to a different issue class.
